title: Bidriware
description: Bidriware is the signature metalcraft associated with Bidar: a blackened zinc-and-copper alloy inlaid with silver, with historic and living production across parts of the Deccan.
dedication: In memory of the Asaf Jahi dynasty
subtitle: Bidar · A Deccan tradition of black metal and silver inlay

items.value: Blackened zinc-and-copper alloy inlaid with silver
Bidar and Hyderabad; also documented in Aurangabad
Bidriware is protected through India's Geographical Indications system

blocks.intro: Bidriware is the black-and-silver metalcraft named for Bidar. The craft uses a zinc-and-copper alloy whose surface is engraved and inlaid with silver before being chemically blackened, producing the contrast that defines Bidri work. Bidar remains its principal historic centre, but Government of India craft documentation also records production in Hyderabad and Aurangabad.

sections.sub: Casting, engraving, inlay and controlled blackening
body: Bidriware takes its name from Bidar, which remains the craft's chief historic centre. A zinc-and-copper alloy is cast and worked, patterns are engraved into the surface, and silver is inlaid into the design. The object is then oxidised to darken the base metal while the silver remains bright, creating Bidriware's characteristic black-and-silver contrast.<cite data-ref="handicrafts-bidri handicrafts-process"></cite>

sections.sub: Bidar at the centre of a wider Deccan craft geography
body: Bidar remains the place most closely identified with Bidriware and an important centre of living production. Government of India craft documentation, however, also records Bidri work in Hyderabad and Aurangabad; the tradition is therefore better understood as a craft centred on Bidar rather than one that has existed nowhere else.<cite data-ref="handicrafts-process"></cite>
